categories.name: Ultimate Skills
categories.description: The pinnacle of power. Ultimate Skills reshape battle and self alike.

pages.text:
Type: Ultimate Skill

A living suit of armor that hardens with your power. The plating is fixed at the moment you toggle it on, by your EP then:
- High Magisteel
- Pure Magisteel - 200,000 EP
- Adamantite - 800,000 EP

- Hihiirokane - 1,000,000 EP

Toggle it on to wear the armor - it costs nothing to keep up, but switches itself off the moment you put real armor on. While worn it shields you from magicule poison.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Crocodile Skin**, become a True Demon Lord or True Hero, and reach **10,000,000 EP**.

Learning Basilisk Skin consumes Crocodile Skin.

*Servers may relax these requirements via config.*

Type: Ultimate Skill

The Lord of Gluttony's absorption economy. A six-mode skill built around devouring, storing, and redistributing power:
- Predation
- Stomach
- Isolate
- Food Chain: Provide
- Food Chain: Receive
- Soul Consume
Where Ouroboros wields Gluttony through raw combat, Beelzebuth channels it through consumption, storage, and conversion.

pages.title: Predation & Stomach
pages.text: Hold to unleash a devouring mist that drains magicule, steals skills, and bites for a flat **300** a pulse - killed targets and their dropped items are swept straight into your **Stomach**, a spatial storage **108** slots deep.

pages.title: Isolate
pages.text: A one-way quarantine: sealed items and cleansed debuffs can't be retrieved, only converted. Sneak-press to convert everything held in Isolate into magicule on demand.

pages.title: Food Chain
pages.text: **Provide** grants one of your mastered skills to a subordinate. **Receive** permanently copies a mastered skill from a subordinate in return - a two-way bond.

pages.title: Soul Consume
pages.text: Hold to unleash a Soul Steal aura, instantly reaping the souls of nearby foes whose will has broken. Any hit landed while this mode is active also inflicts Soul Drain.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Gluttony** and **Merciless**, become a True Demon Lord or True Hero, and reach **10,000,000 EP**.

Learning Beelzebuth consumes **Merciless** as its price.

*Servers may relax these requirements via config.*

Type: Ultimate Skill

The land itself answers. Every other Ultimate travels with you unchanged; Gaia is only as strong as the ground beneath your feet is yours.
Evolves from **Earth Wall** and **Stone Shot** (both mastered), and asks that your nation already hold something worth defending. Neither magic is consumed, and learning it costs **no magicule**.

pages.title: Whose Ground
pages.text:
Before anything else, Gaia asks where you stand.


- On your own nation's claim, everything strikes at **160%**.
- On unclaimed land, **60%**.

- Inside another nation's claim, **30%** - unless you are at war with them, and then the land forgets its loyalty and gives you **100%**.

Only the force, reach and duration bend this way. What you *pay* never changes.

pages.title: Tectonic Spikes
pages.text: A widening cone of crystal spikes tears up out of the ground ahead of you, throwing whatever they catch into the air.

**72** damage and **19 blocks** of reach on your own soil (a base 45 and 12, scaled by whose land you stand on - 27 and 7 in the wild, half that again on hostile ground). The spikes stand for **10 seconds** and then sink away on their own.
Cast over water or open air and nothing rises - and nothing is spent. Costs **3,000** magicule. **8s** cooldown.

pages.title: Stone Grasp
pages.text: Stone closes on one quarry within **32 blocks** and holds it where it stands - **8 seconds** on your own soil, 5 at war, less elsewhere - and crushes it in one blow as spikes ring its feet: **96** on your own soil, 60 at war, 36 in the wild, 18 on hostile ground.

It cannot walk away. It can still turn, still strike, still work its own arts - this binds the legs, not the will.

Costs **12,000** magicule. **35s** cooldown.

pages.title: Sculpt
pages.text: Raises or lowers a **3x3** patch of earth by one layer where you look - sneak to lower it. Unlike the spikes, this change is **permanent**.

It works *only* inside your own nation's claim, and only on plain earth and stone. It will not touch a chest, a machine, or anything another builder set down.

Costs **800** magicule. **2s** cooldown.

pages.title: Vein Bloom
pages.text: Coaxes ore out of the bare stone already beneath you - iron, copper and coal most often, gold rarer still, and diamond rarest of all.

This is a trade, not a gift. Each vein drawn out costs **400** of the *chunk's own* magicule, and a single patch of ground will yield no more than **12** veins in a day. Bleed the land dry and it gives nothing until it recovers.

Costs **5,000** magicule. **60s** cooldown.

pages.title: Geomancy: Seeding
pages.text: Pours up to **2,000** of your own magicule into the ground you stand on.

On your **own claim** it does more than fill: it deepens the land, raising how much that ground can ever hold by **250**. That deepening *stays*. Seed the same fields long enough and your nation stands on richer earth than anyone else's.

Elsewhere it merely tops the ground up and is forgotten. Nothing takes root near world spawn.

**10s** cooldown.

pages.title: Geomancy: Stripping
pages.text: Sneak instead, and you tear **250** of that depth back out and pocket what the land can no longer keep.

This works on *anyone's* ground, including a rival's carefully tended fields - but every strip that lowers a floor, your own included, burns **a fifth of your maximum magicule**. You will almost always end poorer than you began.

**10s** cooldown.

pages.title: Bulwark of Gaia
pages.text: A toggle apart from the modes. Standing on your own claim, you and every countryman within **12 blocks** are shielded by **Resistance II**.

Step off your land and the shield sleeps - but the earth keeps taking its **1,000** magicule each tick regardless. Lighting it is a decision, not a habit. It snuffs itself out the moment you cannot pay.

pages.title: Weight of the World
pages.text:
The ground never harms its lord. You take **no falling damage**, ever, from any height.

*What you rule cannot wound you.*

Type: Ultimate Skill

The forge answers its lord. Where other Ultimates make you stronger in a fight, Hephaestus makes you stronger at the anvil - and then lets you carry the anvil into the fight.
Evolves from **Creator** and **Godly Craftsman** (both mastered). Neither is consumed, and learning it costs **no magicule**.

pages.title: Reforge
pages.text: Mends the item in your hand to whole. If it came from a Forge station, its quality is *rerolled* from nothing - a fresh score between **35** and **95**. The old worth is not remembered, for good or ill.
Costs **8,000** magicule, plus **4** more for every point of damage mended. **120s** cooldown.

pages.title: Engrave
pages.text:
Opens the engraving choice for the held item and burns one mark into it.

Costs a flat **6,000** magicule, paid as the choice opens; the mark it burns is always level 1. **90s** cooldown.

pages.title: Conjure Arms
pages.text:
Draws a blade out of nothing, bound to your soul. It lasts **5 minutes** and unmakes itself the moment you drop it.

Its quality climbs with your forging mastery - **one rank per 8 levels**. A novice conjures a novice's sword.
Costs **25,000** magicule. **10 minute** cooldown.

pages.title: Hammer of Creation
pages.text:
A hammerfall in a **5 block** cone, striking everything before you.

Damage is **12** base, **+0.8** for each level of forging mastery, and **+6** for every quality rank of the finest thing you have ever made.
The smith's whole life swings with the hammer. Costs **4,000** magicule. **4s** cooldown.

pages.title: Chains of Hephaestus
pages.text:
Binds the nearest quarry within a **12 block** cone where it stands, for **6 seconds**.

Costs **10,000** magicule. **30s** cooldown.

pages.title: Ore Sense
pages.text:
A toggle apart from the modes. Every ore within **24 blocks** glows through solid stone - including magic ore mother rock.

It drains **150** magicule each tick and snuffs itself out with a warning the moment you cannot pay.

pages.title: Divine Hand
pages.text:
Once per day, the first forge stage you play scores a flawless **100/100**. You still swing the hammer; the result was decided before you did.

*The forge guides your hand.*

pages.title: Nation Forge Boon
pages.text:
While you are online and sworn to a nation, **every** online member of that nation forges better - a flat **+3 forge quality**, all of them, all the time.

It costs you nothing and has no daily limit. A nation with a Lord of Creation in it simply makes finer things than one without.

Type: Ultimate Skill

The serpent that devours its own tail. Where Beelzebuth turns hunger outward, Ouroboros turns it inward - self-consumption that fuels endless renewal.
Evolves from **Survivor** and **Gourmet** (both mastered). Neither is consumed - the serpent takes nothing but its own tail.

pages.title: Eternal Renewal
pages.text:
Toggle. While active, a share of the damage you deal returns to you as flesh and magicule - but your strikes land softer.

The serpent feeds on the fight itself. The icon shows while the feast lasts.

pages.title: Timeless Fangs
pages.text:
Prime the fangs, then strike: your next blow bites three times - once now, twice more across the following seconds, each echo harder than the last.

The echoes pierce armor and belong to no one.

pages.title: Molt
pages.text:
Shed your skin: severance and every affliction are cast off, and new scales harden over you - golden hearts that grow with what you shed.

Your own Cycle Debt clings too deep to molt away.

pages.title: Coil Back
pages.text:
The coil remembers. One press returns you to where you stood five seconds ago and mends half of what you lost on the way.

The serpent does not undo the past; it slithers back along it.

pages.title: Cycle's End
pages.text: Pay half your greatest magicule to arm the cycle - the mark shows how long it holds. Die while it holds and you die in truth: the price is paid, and then you rise where you fell, diminished, bearing Cycle Debt that stacks with each rebirth.
A severed soul cannot complete the circle.

pages.title: Serpent's Maw
pages.text: The serpent's jaws close on everything before you: a bite that strikes all in a cone ahead, dealing heavy damage plus a share of each victim's greatest health - and a quarter of all it takes returns to you as flesh.
An empty bite costs nothing. The maw does not snap at air.
Type: Ultimate Skill

The Lord of Wisdom — a battlefield-computation entity. Power flows from **Analysis**: mark a target with Analyze, then Prediction can negate their attacks, the Multilayer Barrier hardens against them, and Reverse-Engineer reconstructs their skills — no luck involved.
**Shift-press** Analyze to cycle appraisal vision: Off, Entities, Blocks, Both.

pages.title: Independent Counsel
pages.text: Raphael watches the battle and **proposes** actions — deploying the barrier when your vitals drop, engaging Prediction when an analyzed hostile closes in. Press the skill key while a proposal is pending to approve it.
Against a lethal blow, Raphael acts on its own: an emergency defense leaves you at 1 HP, at a heavy magicule cost.

pages.title: Ars Magna & Workshop
pages.text: Instant casting, chant annulment and halved magicule costs apply only while a **computed situation** exists — a live analysis, Prediction, or the barrier running.
The Sage's Workshop mode bundles the artisan facilities: spatial storage, research enchanting, refining, repeat crafting, Degenerate crafting and synthesis/separation (sneak to cycle).

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master both **Great Sage** and **Godly Craftsman**, become a True Demon Lord or True Hero, and reach **10,000,000 EP**.

*Servers may relax these requirements via config.*

Type: Ultimate Skill

Dominion over the void. Open a void domain, strike with a null slash, dash through space with Event Horizon, and collapse the souls of those caught within.

Evolves from Void Edge.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Void Edge** (itself only ever granted by an operator), become a True Demon Lord or True Hero, reach **10,000,000 EP**, and pay **50,000** magicule.

Learning Void Sovereign consumes Void Edge - the blade becomes the throne.
*Servers may relax these requirements via config.*

categories.name: Unique Skills
categories.description: Rare Skills born of a singular will, often the seed of greater power.

pages.text: Type: Unique Skill

Brain gives a creature a working mind. Any mob holding this skill starts using everything it knows the way a player would - keeping its defensive skills switched on, pressing its combat skills when threatened, and casting its learned spells in battle.

pages.title: How It Fights
pages.text: Every few seconds the mob sizes up its situation. In a fight it hurls its strongest direct-damage magic at its target - fire, ice, lightning and the like come first, trickier control spells second. When it drops below **half health**, it switches to healing magic instead.
Spells cost the mob real magicule - when it runs dry, the casting stops.

pages.title: Reading the Signs
pages.text: A casting mob telegraphs: a **magic circle** appears above its head, colored to match the element it is about to unleash, and the spell launches from the circle itself. That flash is your window - interrupt it, shield up, or get out of the line of fire.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text: Granted by an operator only, and meant for mobs, not players - on a player it simply sits inert. Use it to turn a named guard, boss, or pet into a genuine spellcaster: teach the mob skills and magic, then grant it Brain and let it think for itself.

Type: Unique Skill

Scaled hide that toughens as your EP grows, granting tiered armor while toggled on.

Evolves from Dragon Skin, and can itself grow toward greater skins.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Dragon Skin** and reach **1,000 EP**.

Learning Crocodile Skin consumes Dragon Skin.

**Elder Soul** is a primordial soul in full bloom - the Unique evolution of Ancient Soul.

Its aura reaches **40 blocks** (**50** mastered), granting allies **Strength III**, **Regeneration III** and **Resistance II**.

pages.title: Revealing Presence
pages.text:
Every hostile creature - and enemy player - inside your aura is outlined with a glow *all* your allies can see, lingering a moment after they slip out.

Your Soul Sight reaches 50 blocks. Drain: 4 magicules/tick.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Ancient Soul**, reach **100,000 EP** and defeat **5 bosses** (Tensura bosses or world calamities), then learn it for 1,000 magicules.

Learning Elder Soul consumes Ancient Soul.

**Fortune's Eye** is the Scavenger's instinct honed into true sight - a Unique evolution.

Permanent **Luck III** (**Luck IV** mastered) - no toggle, always on.

pages.title: Loot Sense
pages.text:
Press to reveal every dropped item within **24 blocks** (**40** mastered) with a glowing outline through walls, for 10 seconds.

Costs 100 magicules; cooldown 60 s (30 mastered).

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Scavenger**, reach **100,000 EP** and defeat **5 bosses** (Tensura bosses or world calamities), then learn it for 1,000 magicules.

Learning Fortune's Eye consumes Scavenger.

Type: Unique Skill

Hecate, goddess of magic. In your skill slot, nearly every spell you cast costs only **10%** of its normal magicule - Reincarnation is the one exception, kept at full price.

pages.title: Toggle
pages.text:
Toggling Hecate on grants instant casting with no chant needed, faster skill learning and mastery gain, and **+30** bonus damage to all your spell damage (**+75** once mastered).

Draws **50 magicule** per tick while active - toggles off on its own if you run dry.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text: Granted by an operator only - Hecate is not learned through normal growth.

**Stillness** is Meditation perfected - a Unique evolution.

**Serenity** (toggle): aura, magicule and spiritual-health regeneration at double Meditation's rate - triple once mastered - for 30 magicules/tick.

pages.title: Inner Calm
pages.text:
Switch to the second mode and press: instantly restore **25%** of your MAX magicules and aura (**40%** mastered).

Cooldown 5 minutes (3 mastered). Free to cast.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Meditation**, reach **50,000 EP** and defeat **3 bosses** (Tensura bosses or world calamities), then learn it for 1,000 magicules.

Learning Stillness consumes Meditation.

**Unbreakable** is Iron Resolve tempered until it refuses to break - all four arts, sharpened:
- **Vein Sense** - Haste X
- **Iron Aegis** - up to **50%** damage reduction at full magicules
- **Resolute Surge** - Strength IV, 5 min (10 mastered)

pages.title: Undying Will
pages.text:
Arm the fourth mode: a blow that would kill you is refused - you survive at **10%** health with 3 seconds of full immunity and an automatic Surge.

Once per **10 minutes** (6 mastered). The void and /kill ignore it.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Master **Iron Resolve**, reach **150,000 EP** and defeat **8 bosses** (Tensura bosses or world calamities), then learn it for 1,000 magicules.

Learning Unbreakable consumes Iron Resolve.

Type: Unique Skill

Cloak yourself in the void and hurl void projectiles at your enemies.

This skill is the precursor to the Void Sovereign ultimate.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Granted by an operator or in Creative mode - it is not learned through normal growth.

Note: the Void Edge *sword* is a separate weapon item, not this skill.

categories.name: Extra Skills
categories.description: Refined techniques that sharpen body, mind, and fortune.

pages.text:
Type: Extra Skill

Toggle on to bathe nearby allies in an ancient aura - Strength III, Regeneration III, and Resistance I - while you gain Soul Sight to read the souls around you.
Drains magicule while active. Learning it demands great EP and 25 resets.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text: Reach **5,000 EP** and have reset at least **25 times**.
**Evolution:** master Ancient Soul, reach **100,000 EP** and defeat **5 bosses** to evolve it into **Elder Soul** - a far wider aura that also reveals every enemy inside it.

Type: Extra Skill

A four-mode discipline of body and will:
- Vein Sense - Haste
- Iron Aegis - damage reduction scaled to EP
- Resolute Surge - Strength
- Last Stand - endure a killing blow

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text: Granted by an operator or in Creative mode.
**Evolution:** master Iron Resolve, reach **150,000 EP** and defeat **8 bosses** to evolve it into **Unbreakable** - a 50% Aegis, Strength IV Surge, and a once-per-cooldown refusal to die.

Type: Extra Skill

Center yourself to accelerate the regeneration of aura, magicule, and spiritual health.

Toggle on to begin; it slowly drains magicule while active.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text: Reach **500 EP**.
**Evolution:** master Meditation, reach **50,000 EP** and defeat **3 bosses** to evolve it into **Stillness** - doubled regeneration and an instant recovery burst.

Type: Extra Skill

Fortune favors you. Passively grants Luck II.

Once mastered, toggle the skill on to raise your fortune to Luck III.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Granted by an operator or in Creative mode.

Once held, its passive Luck works for everyone; only mastered holders can toggle the Luck III boost.
**Evolution:** master Scavenger, reach **100,000 EP** and defeat **5 bosses** to evolve it into **Fortune's Eye** - permanent Luck III and a loot-revealing pulse.

categories.name: Intrinsic Skills
categories.description: Innate, body-born abilities. The two Mechanical skills require the Create mod to be installed.

pages.text: Type: Intrinsic Skill

A Saiyan's defiant technique - burn your life force to multiply your power in a blazing crimson aura. While it holds, your **magicule and aura** swell far past their limit and your strength, armor and speed surge with them. The red aura wraps your whole body in flame.

pages.title: Ranks
pages.text:
Kaioken has four ranks, each a greater multiplier:
- **Kaioken** - double energy
- **Kaioken x3**
- **Kaioken x10**
- **Kaioken x20**
Higher ranks open as your **EP** grows: x3 at **100,000**, x10 at **1,000,000**, and x20 at **10,000,000** - and only once the skill is **mastered**. Cycle to the rank you can bear before you ignite.
The aura itself tells the tale: deep blood red at first, then orange, then gold, and white-hot at x20 - anyone watching can read how far you have pushed.

pages.title: The Toll
pages.text: Power like this devours you. While Kaioken burns it drains your **health and energy** every moment, though never enough on its own to kill you. It lasts up to **3 minutes** - **6** once mastered - then burns out.

pages.title: Exhaustion
pages.text: When the aura fades your body pays: **Weakness, Fragility and Paralysis** for about **10 minutes**. You **cannot** ignite Kaioken again until that exhaustion clears, and it will not stack with any other transformation.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text: Kaioken is not learned - it is **born into you**. It comes to **Medium Saiyans** and the greater Saiyan forms beyond, with no cost to acquire.

Type: Intrinsic Skill

Requires the Create mod to be installed.

Your eyes gain the sight of Create's engineer's goggles, revealing stress and contraption information.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Requires the **Create** mod to be installed.

With Create present, reach **25,000 EP**.

Type: Intrinsic Skill

Requires the Create mod to be installed.

Your hands act as a Create wrench. Two modes let you rotate or remove any wrenchable contraption block.

pages.title: How to Unlock
pages.text:
Requires the **Create** mod to be installed.

With Create present, reach **25,000 EP**.

categories.name: Races
categories.description: Bloodlines and the power they grant.

pages.text:
The Saiyan bloodline - a warrior race that grows stronger with every battle and brush with death.

Saiyans ascend through four tiers of raw power:
- Lesser Saiyan
- Medium Saiyan
- High Saiyan
- Divine Saiyan
Each tier raises combat potential and unlocks greater strength.

categories.name: Forge
categories.description: Craft legendary gear at the forge.

pages.text: **Aetherforged** gear is Star-Iron - near-black plate veined with cyan light, forged from Hihiirokane under conditions only a **Dragonforge** station can reach.

Four weapons and a four-piece armor set. Every piece comes only from the forge, so quality, engravings and the minigame all apply.

*Nothing here needs a skill or race - if you can run a Dragonforge, you can wear it.*

pages.title: The Weapons
pages.text:
Each weapon carries one **signature active** on right-click, paid in aura and magicule:
- **Spear** - *Piercing Vector*: hold to charge (up to 1.5s), release to lunge and thrust 6 blocks for 1.5x-3x your attack. 300/300, 8s

- **Katana** - *Phase Cut*: arms the blade for 5s; the next hit adds half your attack as armor-ignoring phase damage. 250/250, 10s
- **War Hammer** - *Crushing Impact*: slam a 4-block ring for 1.2x attack, knock-up and Slowness II. 400/400, 12s
- **Gauntlets** - *Aether Burst*: a 3.5-block shockwave for 0.8x attack that hurls everything outward. 200/200, 8s

pages.title: Cooldown Panel
pages.text: Every Aetherforged weapon, plus the Void Edge and Astral Edge swords, reports to one **Gear Cooldowns** panel above your hotbar. Gear in your hands is listed in white with every mode; gear stowed in the hotbar gets one grey line each, soonest ready first.

Each row shows the item, the ability name, a bar that fills as the cooldown runs down, and the seconds left - or **READY**.

Nothing is drawn when you carry none of this gear. Move the panel from the mod list's **Config** button, under HUD Positions.

pages.title: Aetherforged Plate
pages.text: The armor sits a full step above Hihiirokane in every number - defense, toughness, knockback resistance and durability - and every piece is a fresh canvas for forge engravings.

Wear all **four** pieces and the set answers your power: incoming damage is cut by up to **25%**, scaling with your EP and reaching its peak at ten million.

The gauntlets are worn, not held - they show as bracers on your arms.

pages.title: Forging It
pages.text:
All recipes are **Dragonforge** tier:
- Each armor piece - the matching Hihiirokane piece + 2 Hihiirokane ingots + 2 Orichalcum ingots
- Spear / Katana - the Hihiirokane spear or katana + 2 Hihiirokane + 2 Orichalcum

- War Hammer - 4 Hihiirokane + 2 Pure Magisteel + 2 Earth cores
- Gauntlets - 4 Hihiirokane + 2 Pure Magisteel + 2 Space cores

The finished Hihiirokane input is consumed - you are reforging it, not copying it.
Every recipe also needs **Star Iron**: 4 for each weapon, 3 for chestplate/leggings, 2 for helmet/boots. It only falls during a **Starfall** event - see that entry.

Twenty-eight custom **engravings** join the base engraving pool - 22 beneficial and 6 **cursed**. Gear earns them three ways:
- **EP growth** - when a piece crosses a major EP threshold and a Rare or Epic engraving would roll, there is a 25% chance it becomes a custom one instead

- **Forge crafting** - quality crafts come pre-engraved from a much larger pool
- **Curses** - half of the game's own curse rolls, and forge crafts that fire two critical upgrades, may pick up a cursed engraving

pages.title: EP Rolls: Armor
pages.text:
The roll must be one of the game's Rare or Epic engravings; the item's **slot** then decides the pool. On **armor** it can become:
- **Magicule Conduit** - +25% magicule regen per level (max 4)
- **Aura Conduit** - +25% aura regen per level (max 4)
- **Featherfall** - -25% fall damage per level, boots (max 2)

pages.title: EP Rolls: Weapons
pages.text:
On **hand-held gear** it can become:
- **Frostbrand** - slows on hit (max 4)
- **Vampiric** - heal 8% of damage per level (max 5)
- **Voidpiercer** - bonus damage scaling with the target's armor (max 5)

- **Executioner** - +10%/level vs targets under 30% health (max 3)
- **Rending** - shreds 2 armor per level for a few seconds (max 3)

pages.title: Forge-Only
pages.text: Fourteen more only come from the forge: **Keen Edge**, **Featherweight**, **Reinforced**, **Toughened**, **Vitality**, **Swiftness**, and **Regeneration** (self-repair).

The rest: **Critical Strike**, **Soulbound** (kept on death), **Soul Render** (vs spiritual), **Stormbrand** (lightning arcs), **Predator's Mark** (+kill EP), **Cleave** (splash hits), and **Prospector** (duplicate drops).

pages.title: Cursed
pages.text:
Six **cursed** engravings trade a real drawback for a real edge - one curse per item at most, never above level 1, and a grindstone will not strip them:
- **Blood Pact** - +20% melee damage, each hit costs 2 HP (never lethal)

- **Berserker's Brand** - +30% melee below half health, +25% damage taken
- **Mana Thirst** - +20% melee while each hit drains 250 magicule; -20% when you cannot pay
- **Iron Maiden** - +4 armor +3 toughness, -15% speed
- **Parasite Skin** - +10 max HP +50% magicule regen, healing -75%
- **Thorn Pact** - reflect 15% melee, +10% damage taken

pages.title: From the Forge
pages.text: Quality forge work fills its engraving slots automatically - **Superior 1**, **Masterwork 2**, **Legendary 3**, **Mythical 4** - matched to the item: weapons get weapon engravings, armor gets armor engravings. Better minigame scores mean higher engraving levels.
Craft engravings survive gear evolution and stack with ones earned later through EP.
Each forge recipe defines its **ingredients**, the minimum station **tier** it needs, which **minigames** you must clear, and what it produces.
Recipes are **data-driven**: packs can add or tweak them, and they hot-reload with */reload*. Some stay hidden until discovered.

pages.title: Quality
pages.text:
Every craft earns a **Quality** rank from how well you forge:
- Poor, Common, Fine, Superior, Masterwork
- Legendary & Mythical - only via lucky *critical upgrades*
Higher quality means stronger stats, more durability, and more **engraving slots** (Superior 1 -> Mythical 4).

pages.title: Engravings
pages.text: Each engraving slot is filled with an **engraving** matched to the item - weapons draw from the weapon pool, armor from the armor pool. See the **Engravings** entry for the full list.

Slot count comes from quality, plus extras from your skills and titles. Better minigame scores mean **higher engraving levels**.

Gear forged before this system converts automatically and keeps its power.

pages.title: Boosting Your Craft
pages.text:
Your quality, slot count, and levels improve with:
- A high minigame **score**
- Crafting skills like *Godly Craftsman*
- Titles, synergies, and a forge **specialization** (weaponsmith, armorsmith...)

Admins manage recipes with */etadmin forge*.
**Runesmith's Insight** is the smith's own skill - the one thing at the forge you cannot buy, trade, or learn with Existence Points.
It arrives on its own. Finish **25** successful crafts and it is simply yours, with no prompt and no cost. Nothing you do at the anvil is wasted; the count only ever goes up.

pages.title: At the Anvil
pages.text:
From the moment you hold it, every forging minigame gets kinder.


- The sweet spot is **25%** wider, so the band you are aiming for is easier to hit.
- Heat drains **25%** slower, giving you more time before the temperature drifts out from under you.
Both apply the instant a craft begins. There is nothing to switch on.

pages.title: Mastery
pages.text: Every successful forge after you learn it adds one mastery point. Keep working and it masters itself.

A **mastered** Runesmith's Insight gives each craft a **25%** chance of one *extra engraving slot* - a free roll at another property on the finished piece, on top of everything your other skills grant.
It stacks with Godly Craftsman, Researcher, Analyst and the rest. They are not alternatives to each other.

pages.title: Notes
pages.text:
The skill sits in your list but has no button and no active use - it works entirely on its own while you craft.

Forging is on by default. If an admin has turned it off with the **ETForgeEnabled** gamerule, nothing at the anvil progresses, this skill included.
Every Forge Station has a **Salvage** button next to Specialize. It works on any forged item except Aetherforged gear and Conjured items - no skill needed.
This is separate from Hephaestus's Reforge and Engrave, which stay skill-gated. Salvage and Reroll are open to everyone at the station.

pages.title: Salvaging
pages.text:
Salvage destroys the item and refunds part of its recipe's ingredients - **20%** at Poor up to **75%** at Mythical. Tag ingredients refund nothing.

Weapon Legend kill history is lost with the item.
Each engraving on it has a **25%** chance to yield one **Engraving Scroll** capturing that engraving and its level, up to one scroll per salvage. Cursed engravings are never captured.

pages.title: Engraving Scroll
pages.text:
Off-hand a forged item with a free slot and use the scroll: it applies the captured engraving at its level and is consumed.

Refuses a full item, an Aetherforged/Conjured item, or an engraving it can't hold.

pages.title: Rerolling
pages.text: Reroll swaps one engraving for a different random one at the same level, for materials (about a quarter of the recipe) plus cash on banking-enabled servers, scaled by rank.
Capped at **3 rerolls** per item - the count survives a Hephaestus Reforge. Rerolling never touches Weapon Legend.

The Forge lets you craft powerful, one-of-a-kind gear by hand rather than on a crafting table.

Interact with a Forge Station block to open the forge and choose a recipe.
Enabled by the ETForgeEnabled gamerule (on by default).
Craft a **Basic Forge Station** from 8 iron ingots around an anvil. Place it, then right-click to open the forge.

pages.title: Station Upgrades
pages.text:
A station levels up on its own as you complete crafts on it:
- Basic - **20** crafts -> Magisteel
- Magisteel - **40** crafts -> Mythril
- Mythril - **80** crafts -> Dragonforge

On reaching the count, the station upgrades in place with a flourish and its craft counter resets.

Higher tiers can craft everything the lower tiers can, and they raise the minigame difficulty for tougher gear.
*Server-configurable - a threshold of 0 disables that upgrade step.*

pages.title: Nation Bonuses
pages.text:
A station in your nation's own territory needs fewer crafts to upgrade, the discount growing with your nation's level.

The **Forge Boon** nation perk goes further, raising the quality and crit chance of every craft made inside that territory.

Forging is a minigame. Each recipe runs you through challenges you must clear well to craft a quality result:
- Hammer Timing - strike on rhythm
- Dragonfire Forging - work the bellows to keep the heat in the hot band, then strike
- Rune Alignment - line up the runes
- Magicule Flow - steady the flow of power (this one drains real magicule up front)
The better you perform across each challenge, the higher the quality of the gear you forge. Rush it and the result suffers.

Score also feeds **critical upgrades** - a perfect run adds up to +15% crit chance - and sets a floor: score **90+** guarantees at least Fine, **98+** at least Superior. Difficulty follows the *recipe* tier, not the station.

Forged weapons remember. Every hostile creature or player you slay with a forged weapon in hand is carved into its history - and the weapon grows a **legend**.

Passive animals don't count. Neither does anything killed bare-handed.

pages.title: Legend Tiers
pages.text:
- **Blooded** - 100 kills: the weapon's story appears in its tooltip
- **Renowned** - 1,000 kills: a ✯ joins its name
- **Legendary** - 10,000 kills: the name turns gold with ✯✯

Thresholds are server-configurable.

pages.title: Slayer of Giants
pages.text:
Boss kills - the world's counted bosses and this server's calamity horrors - are tallied separately.

At **25 boss kills** the weapon earns **one extra engraving**, chosen by fate. Once per weapon, ever.

A legend never fades: reforging and gear evolution keep the tally.

Anvil names are respected - your "Cabbage Slicer" stays the Cabbage Slicer, stars and all in its tooltip.

Every earned Record grants a **permanent bonus** - and unlike titles, there are no slots to manage. All of your Record bonuses are *always active*.

Bonuses include:
- Attribute boosts
- Status effects
- Skill-mastery gains

pages.title: Ever Stronger
pages.text:
Records come in seven rarities - Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic, **Divine**.

The more Records you write, the permanently stronger you become - a reward no reset can take away.

**Records** are a permanent chronicle of your journey. Once earned, a Record is yours *forever* - it survives prestige resets and even death.

Enabled by the **ETRecordsEnabled** gamerule (on by default).

pages.title: Records vs Titles
pages.text:
Records mirror the Title system, but with one big difference - they are **never wiped** and never need equipping. Their rewards are simply always on.

They are grouped into categories:
- Combat & Exploration
- Crafting & Nation
- Social & World Event

Each Record lists **conditions** - feats the game tracks for you automatically. Meet every condition and the Record is written at once.

Examples:
- Kills, EP reached, deaths survived
- Biomes & structures found, distance walked

- Skills learned/mastered, forge crafts
- Calamities slain, wars won, Walpurgis attended

pages.title: World-First Records
pages.text:
Some Records are a race. The **first player ever** to achieve one claims the **World First** - announced to the entire server by the Voice of the World.

Everyone can still earn the Record afterward; only the first claims the glory.

categories.name: Nations
categories.description: Build, ally, and war with FTB-team nations.

pages.text:
Nations shape the world through diplomacy - **alliances** and **wars**.

**Alliances** are pacts between nations. Allies may join your wars.
How many you can hold depends on your Reputation tier - from **5** at Exalted down to **none** while rogue. Forming one grants both nations reputation; **breaking** one costs the breaker dearly.

pages.title: Declaring War
pages.text:
There is **no accept step**. Your Sovereign declares, and the war begins: */etnation war declare <player>*.

Declaring costs treasury cash, **+25%** for every level you are above your target.

You are blocked if you are rogue, at your war cap, allied to them, or they are under **loser grace** from a recent defeat.

Declaring on a much weaker nation is **bullying** - allowed, but it costs reputation.

pages.title: The Campaign
pages.text:
A war is a race for **war score**, not a fight to the death.


- **Warmup** - 24h, no scoring. Allies may join
- **Active** - 72h, scoring live
- **Resolution** - spoils and standing
- **Cooldown** - 2h before you may clash again

The loser also gets **24h of grace** where nobody may declare on them.

Follow it with */etnation war status*.

pages.title: Scoring
pages.text:
- Enemy kill - **10** points
- Kill inside their claims - **doubled**
- Repeat kill on one victim - decays to a quarter
- **Regicide** (their Sovereign) - 50
- **First Blood** - 15
- **Rampage** (3 victims) - 30

- A Masterwork+ forge craft while the war runs - scales with quality

*Raiding pays double. Farming one player does not pay at all. Crafters contribute without fighting.*

Objectives rotate every 4 hours for both sides.

pages.title: Bounties
pages.text: Your Sovereign may escrow treasury cash on an enemy's head: */etnation war bounty <player> <amount>* - minimum **$1000**.

Any killer on your side takes the **whole escrow** into their bank, plus 20 points for the side. Re-placing tops it up; unclaimed cash refunds when the war ends.

*These are separate from the public bounty board.*

pages.title: Victory & Spoils
pages.text:
At the deadline the **higher score wins**. A tie is a draw with no spoils. A side may also */etnation war surrender* once the war is active (not during warmup).

The victor loots a share of the loser's **treasury** - paid to the winning nation itself, not its allies.

Winning grants reputation, with a bonus if you were the **defender**. Losing or surrendering costs it.

*Treasury withdrawals are locked during a war - build your war chest before you declare.*

pages.title: On the Map
pages.text:
While a war of yours is warming up or active, the enemy's claimed land turns **war-red** on the FTB Chunks map - the large map, the minimap and the claim screen all show it.

Your own and every ally's **Nation Core** is pinned too; the enemy's is pinned as well until the war ends.

Hover a Core pin for the nation's name, its tier, and whether it's shattered. A nation hiding its claims never tints - its land just reads as unclaimed.

You can turn these map markers off for yourself in the mod's config, and your server can disable the whole overlay too.

pages.title: Ley Nexus
pages.text: While a war is **Active**, **1-3 Ley Nexus** crystals rise on unclaimed ground between the two nations. Stand within **16 blocks** to fill its capture meter for your side - majority presence wins it, ties freeze it, and about **60s** of unopposed control captures or flips it.

Holding a Nexus pays your nation **2 war points** every minute a holder of yours stands inside it - an empty site holds control but pays nothing.

Sites show on your war panel and the FTB map, and the Voice of the World announces when one appears or changes hands. They vanish when the war ends.

pages.title: Peace Terms
pages.text: Win a war outright and your Sovereign has **24h** to set lasting peace terms on the loser, from the Codex Diplomacy tab or */etnation war terms <pact|tribute|vassal>*. How lopsided the win was caps what you can pick.

- **Pact** - always available; neither side may declare on the other
- **Tribute** - needs a **1.25x** score win; pact plus a daily cut of the loser's income

- **Vassalage** - needs **2x**; tribute plus the vassal can't declare war, auto-joins its liege's wars, and the liege auto-joins wars declared on it

A surrender always counts as a rout, opening every tier.

Leave it unpicked and the loser gets an automatic pact.

Terms run **7 days**. Tribute is **10%** of the loser's hourly income x24 (minimum $200/day) - skipped, never taken on debt, if they can't pay.
A liege may free their vassal early: */etnation war release <nation>*. */etnation war terms* alone shows your nation's current terms. Active terms also show on Discord's !nation.

The **contract board** is server-wide. Nations post jobs; anyone can take them.

Open it with */etcontract gui*.

Two kinds of posting share the board:
- **Delivery contracts** - bring us N of an item
- **Bounties** - kill this player
*It is the main way nations deal with players who are not their citizens.*

pages.title: Deliveries
pages.text:
A nation asks for an item and count, backed by treasury cash, an escrowed item stack, or both.

**Anyone may fulfil one** - including players with no nation at all.
Matching is by **item type and count only**. Durability, enchantments and custom names are ignored, so a worn enchanted pickaxe satisfies a request for one pickaxe. *Post accordingly.*

pages.title: Bounties
pages.text:
A nation posts on a named **online** player. Whoever kills them first is paid **automatically** - no claim step.

Four rules keep them honest:
- The killer must **not** be in the posting nation - checked at the kill
- Nor may the target

- **One open bounty per target** - the same nation may top it up, another nation must wait
- The kill must be a **direct player kill** - void, fall, lava and mobs pay nothing

*Members of a nation currently at war with the poster cannot fulfil its contracts.*

pages.title: Posting
pages.text:
You must be in a founded nation and hold a high enough rank.

From the board, the header shows **+ Contract** and **+ Bounty** buttons. They open a form where you pick the requirement and reward straight from your inventory grid.

*Nothing moves when you click - the form uses ghost slots, so closing it can never lose or duplicate an item.*

Commands still work: */etcontract post|postbounty|list|cancel|fulfil*.

pages.title: Refunds
pages.text:
Contracts expire on a timer. Cancelled, expired and disbanded-nation postings all refund the same way: **cash to the treasury, items to whoever posted them**.

Nations have a cap on open contracts, and some servers block posting during a war.
*A war bounty and a board bounty can sit on the same victim at once - a qualifying kill pays both.*

pages.title: Posting on Your Own
pages.text: You do not need a nation to use the board. **Any player** may post a delivery or a bounty, funded from their own bank and inventory instead of a treasury - the board marks these rows *(player)* instead of a nation name.

Personal posts ignore nation war locks, and you may have up to **3** open at once. Several players may each place a bounty on the same target - every row stacks, and a kill pays out **every bounty the killer qualifies for** at once (never their own, never their nation's).

Personal bounty cash always pays **1:1**, and any refund returns straight to your bank.

*Nation members who outrank a Citizen see a Treasury / My bank toggle on the posting forms; everyone else always posts personally.*

A **Nation** is your FTB team raised into a power on the world stage. The team owner rules as **Sovereign**; the rest become citizens.

Nations gain levels, claim land, earn achievements, build reputation, forge alliances, and wage war.
Off by default - a server enables it with the **ETNationSystem** gamerule.

pages.title: Founding a Nation
pages.text:
First form an FTB party and claim a little land. Then, as the team owner, run **/etnation found**.

You need at least **2 members** *AND* **1 claimed chunk**.
The nation starts at Level 1. Its alignment is taken from you: Demon Lord -> Demonic, True Hero -> Heroic, otherwise Neutral.

pages.title: Roles & Commands
pages.text:
Ranks come straight from your FTB team:
- **Sovereign** - the ruler (found, disband, capital)
- **Officer** - may set the capital
- **Citizen** - a member

Use **/etnation**:
- *info* / *gui* - view your nation
- *score* - level & score breakdown
- *setcapital*, *list*, *disband*

pages.title: Growing Stronger
pages.text:
A nation's **level** (max 20) is driven by a score that rewards almost everything you do together:
- Members & claimed territory
- Total member EP
- Awakened members, True Heroes, Demon Lords
- Records earned & world events joined
- Nation achievements
The score updates on its own - check it with */etnation score*.

pages.title: Rewards & Glory
pages.text: Each level grants more **claim chunks** (about 4 per level), so growing literally widens your borders.

**Achievements** unlock nation-wide bonuses for members, and the first nation to reach certain feats seizes a **World Record** announced to everyone - Largest Territory, Most Citizens, Most Demon Lords, Mightiest Nation.

pages.title: Your Story
pages.text: Every founded nation keeps its own **History** - a ledger of what shaped it: founding, level-ups, members joining and leaving, wars won and lost, alliances made and broken, wonders raised, the Core rising or falling, achievements earned.

Read it in the Codex Nation tab under **History**, newest first. Up to **100** lines are kept; the oldest fade past that. Names are written down as they were, so a rival that later disbanded still reads right. The ledger ends with the nation.

pages.title: Doctrines
pages.text: From **level 3** a nation may adopt one **doctrine** - a permanent stance with a strength and a weakness. The first choice is free. Changing it later costs **$1,000,000** from the treasury and locks you in for **14 days**.

- **Militarist** - +25% war kill points, but +25% upkeep
- **Mercantile** - +50% treasury interest and +15% territory income, but -25% war kill points
- **Arcane** - the Core's aura is 1.5x stronger, but your spawner mob cap drops 25%
- **Builder** - wonder stages cost 20% less cash, but territory income drops 20%

Each doctrine also tilts your **missions**: objectives that suit it roll twice as often.

Fall into **debt** and the strength switches off while the weakness stays - climb out to get it back.

The Sovereign chooses with */etnation doctrine* - a card with a clickable row per doctrine - or from the **Doctrine** block at the top of the Codex Perks section. Your current doctrine also shows on the Nation overview.

pages.title: Going Further
pages.text:
Three deeper systems build on your nation - each has its own page:
- **Reputation** - your standing, and the diplomacy it gates
- **Alliances & War** - pacts and conflicts
- **Nation Spawners** - level-gated mob spawners

Not every player wants to found or join a nation - so nations are not the only door to their rewards.

While you belong to **no founded nation**, you get your own perks, your own missions, and titles that reward the road alone.
Join or found a nation later and these simply switch off - nothing is lost, they just stand aside.

pages.title: Personal Perks
pages.text:
Buy timed perks straight from your own bank in the Nation screen's Perks section, or */etnation perks buy <id>*:
- *Forge Focus* - wider hammer sweet spots
- *Keen Senses* - +5% magicule & aura gain from kills
- *Wanderer's Stride* - +5% movement speed

- *Hardy* - +2 max health
- *Frugal Hands* - cheaper magicule-flow forge stages

Each lasts a **week**; buying again renews it.

pages.title: Personal Missions
pages.text: You draw **2** missions of your own each cycle - the same cycle nations draw theirs from - covering hunting, forge crafts, EP growth, unlocking titles, and travel.

Clearing one pays cash straight to your bank and a crate key; clearing every mission in the cycle pays a better key on top.

Check them in the Nation screen's Missions tab, or */etnation missions*.

pages.title: The Lone Wolf Line
pages.text:
Three titles reward staying nationless and moving: **Lone Wolf** -> **Wandering Sovereign** -> **Unbound**, each deeper and rarer than the last.

Lone Wolf asks for **7** days spent nationless while online and **5,000** blocks travelled - the days need not be consecutive.
*Joining or founding a nation resets your nationless-day count, so the line is truly for players who stay unaligned.*

pages.title: Home Ground
pages.text: You do not need a nation to claim land, and territory bonuses that key off **your own claims** still work for you.
*Gaia*'s strength on your own soil, for one, honours a personal claim exactly as it would a nation's - you do not need to found or join anything to fight on home ground.

The **Nation Core** is a block your nation places to become a real target and a real anchor - distinct from your capital chunk.

It watches over your land with a standing **aura**, and it can be **besieged** by an enemy nation at war with you.
Only a Sovereign or Officer may raise one, and a nation may only ever have one.

pages.title: Raising a Core
pages.text:
Forge one at a **Dragonforge** station from **8 Hihiirokane Ingots**, **8 Adamantite Ingots**, **16 Magic Stone** and **2 Earth Cores**.

Place it inside your nation's own claimed land. Only a Sovereign or Officer may place it, and only where no core already stands.

Sneak and right-click your core with empty hands for a **status card** - tier, health and the next tier's price, with clickable **Upgrade** and (Sovereign only) **Take down** links. Neither works while a war is warming up or active.

pages.title: The Aura
pages.text:
Standing near an intact core, inside your own nation's claims, grants every member a standing bonus to **magicule/aura regeneration** and **armor**.

The aura reaches out several chunks around the core.
It falls silent if your treasury goes into **debt** - restoring the moment you climb back out.

pages.title: Tiers
pages.text: A core starts at **Tier 1** and can be raised to **Tier 4** from the treasury - **$500,000**, **$1,500,000** and **$3,000,000** by default. Each tier grows its siege health (**5,000** up to **16,000**), its aura reach (**8** up to **14** chunks) and the aura's regeneration and armor.

Buy from the status card, with */etnation core upgrade*, or with the **Upgrade Core** button in the Codex. The block shows its tier: an inner ring at 2, an outer ring at 3, orbiting shards at 4.

A higher tier is also a bigger prize - toppling it hands the attacker more war score.

pages.title: Siege
pages.text:
A nation you are actively at war with may attack your core - **warmup does not count**, only once the war turns active.

A boss bar appears while the core is under attack, with warnings as it crosses **75%**, **50%** and **25%** health remaining.
If it falls, the attacker gains extra war score and a slice of your treasury moves to them once the war resolves - your core stands **shattered** until repaired, and **loses one tier**.

pages.title: Repair
pages.text:
A Sovereign or Officer repairs a damaged or shattered core by right-clicking it while at peace - cost scales with how much health is missing, paid from the treasury.

*Without an active treasury, repairs are free.*
A core that falls in war is also mended automatically once the war ends.

**Missions** are recurring objectives your whole nation works on together.

Every nation rolls at the **same moment**, on a **7-day** cycle, drawing **3** missions filtered to your level.

Open the **Missions** tab of the Nation screen, or use */etnation missions*.

*Missions do not need the banking mod - only their cash rewards do.*

pages.title: Delta & Absolute
pages.text:
At the roll, every nation statistic is snapshotted.


- A **delta** mission asks you to *increase* something - claim 20 more chunks
- An **absolute** mission asks you to *reach* a value - have 8 members
A delta mission cannot be completed by standing still, and cannot be cheesed by having already been large.

pages.title: Frozen Targets
pages.text:
Thresholds are calculated from your population **at the roll** and then frozen.

Recruiting ten people mid-cycle does not move the goalposts - it makes the existing targets *easier*.

Missions **auto-complete**. There is no claim step.
A nation founded mid-cycle sits out until the next roll, starting fresh with everyone else.

pages.title: Rewards
pages.text:
Each mission pays **reputation**, optional **treasury cash**, a **Common Key** to every online member, and **+1** to your missions-completed count.

That counter is permanent and feeds your nation's **score** (and so its level).
Clearing **every** mission in a cycle hands every online member a **Rare Key**; a server may also attach a nation-wide buff until the next roll. A cycle never repeats a mission it rolled last time.

Nation Spawners put your team's **mob spawners** under nation law - stronger nations may run bigger, deadlier spawners.

This only affects **player-placed** spawners. Natural, dungeon, and trial spawners are never touched.
Off by default - a server turns it on with the **ETNationSpawnerSystem** gamerule.

pages.title: How It Works
pages.text:
When a nation member places a spawner, it is claimed for that nation.

Each time it tries to spawn a mob, two checks run:
- The mob must be **unlocked** at your nation's level
- Your nation must be under its **active-mob cap**
Fail either check and that spawn is skipped - the spawner just tries again next cycle.

pages.title: Tier Ladder
pages.text:
Higher nation levels unlock stronger mobs and raise the cap:
- Lvl **1** - cap 4: common beasts, goblins, slimes
- Lvl **5** - cap 8: creepers, orcs, direwolves
- Lvl **10** - cap 12
- Lvl **15** - cap 16

- Lvl **20** - cap 18: apex beasts (megalodon, arch daemon)

The *Spawner Overclock* nation perk counts your nation as one level higher for these checks.

pages.title: Good to Know
pages.text: Unlocks are **cumulative** - your nation can spawn anything from every tier at or below its level, using the cap of its highest unlocked tier.

The cap counts **living** spawner-mobs across your whole nation. Hit it and spawners pause; thin the herd or break a spawner to free room.

*Datapacks can retune the levels, caps, and mob lists.*

A **Wonder** is a multi-stage nation project - build one and every member keeps its bonus for as long as your nation stands.

Six exist. Two of them are **server-unique** - only one nation in the world may ever hold them at a time.
Building one needs an active treasury. Open the Wonders section of the Nation screen, or use */etnation wonder*.

pages.title: Building One
pages.text:
Each Wonder has **three stages**, and each stage needs both treasury cash and deposited items before its build timer starts.
- *start <id>* - begin a project (Sovereign/Officer, one at a time)
- *pay* - spend treasury cash on the current stage

- *contribute* - deposit the held stack, or click a slot in the contribute screen

Once both the cash and items are in, the stage arms and finishes on its own timer. Only your nation's level gates which Wonders you may start.

pages.title: The Six Wonders
pages.text:
- **Grand Forge** - bonus critical upgrades at the forge
- **Aether Spire** - doubles your Nation Core's aura reach and strength
- **War Academy** - more war kill points for every member
- **Hall of Records** - an extra synergy slot and faster EP growth

- **Sanctum of the World** *(unique)* - faster magicule and aura regeneration for **every player alive**
- **Eternal Beacon** *(unique)* - blunts calamity boss damage for **every player alive**

The last two are the server-unique pair - claim one before a rival nation does.

pages.title: Cancelling
pages.text:
Changed your mind mid-build? */etnation wonder cancel* refunds part of the current stage's paid cash.

**Deposited items are never returned** - the game warns you before you confirm.
A finished stage is permanent; only the stage still in progress can be cancelled.

Every nation has a **Reputation** from **-1000** to **+1000**, shown as a tier:
- Reviled, Infamous, Distrusted
- Neutral
- Respected, Honored, Exalted

Left alone, reputation slowly *drifts back toward Neutral* over time.

pages.title: Gaining & Losing
pages.text:
Your deeds move the needle:
- Win a war (more on defense) **+**; lose one **-**
- Bully a far weaker nation **-**
- Form an alliance **+**; break one **-**
- Defend a Calamity, attend a Walpurgis, earn achievements **+**
- Hostile council rulings **-**, friendly ones **+**

pages.title: What It Gates
pages.text:
Your standing opens or closes diplomacy:
- **Rogue** - fall to **-250** or below and you are branded a rogue state
- **War** - you must sit above the war floor to declare
- **Alliances** - your tier caps how many you may hold: Neutral 2, Respected 3, Honored 4, Exalted 5 (Distrusted just 1; lower, none)

A nation can hold money. The **treasury** pays for levels, perks, wars and contracts - and it is drained daily by **upkeep**.

Open the **Treasury** tab of the Nation screen, or use */etnation treasury*.
*This requires the banking mod and must be enabled by your server. Without it, nations level from score alone.*

pages.title: Income
pages.text:
- **Deposits** - */etnation treasury deposit*
- **Pickup tax** - a slice of every member's cash pickup
- **Territory income** - paid periodically, scaling with claimed chunks and level

The pickup tax splits two ways: **5%** to your treasury and **10%** into the central bank reserve - a server-wide money sink.

Territory income never stops, even in debt. That is what makes recovery possible.

pages.title: Spending
pages.text:
**Levels are bought** once the economy runs: */etnation levelup*. You must both qualify by score and pay.

**Perks** are bought from the treasury: */etnation perks buy <id>*.

A few are 1-hour buffs (War Footing, Swift Hands, Stone Skin, Tax Holiday); the rest are permanent upgrades - Veterans' Discount, **Forge Boon**, Spawner Overclock, Golden Ledger, Honored Name, Charter of Industry, Bond of Souls, Deep Pockets, Defender's Resolve, Magicule Attunement.

pages.title: Perks in Detail
pages.text:
- *War Footing* - +10% nation attack, 1h
- *Swift Hands* - Haste I, 1h
- *Stone Skin* - Resistance I, 1h
- *Tax Holiday* - suspends the pickup tax, 1h
- *Veterans' Discount* - halves war declare cost

- *Forge Boon* - better forge quality and crit in your territory
- *Spawner Overclock* - spawners act one level higher
- *Golden Ledger* - more treasury interest


- *Honored Name* - reputation stops decaying

- *Charter of Industry* - one extra mission per cycle
- *Bond of Souls* - larger subordinate EP share
- *Deep Pockets* - more contracts open at once
- *Defender's Resolve* - bonus war points while defending
- *Magicule Attunement* - passive regen in your territory

pages.title: Upkeep
pages.text:
Every day your nation is billed:

**30 per claimed chunk** plus **100 x your level**.

The bill scales with what you hold, so a sprawling empire costs more to run than a compact one.

Two mercies: a period where **nobody logged in** bills at 25%, and after server downtime only one missed period is billed at a time.

Watch the next-bill countdown in the Treasury tab.

pages.title: Debt
pages.text:
**Read this before it happens.**

If a bill lands and you cannot pay, the treasury goes **negative**:
- **Every nation bonus is suspended** - achievements, perks, mission buffs, for every member

- **Every spend is locked** - levels, perks, wars, contracts, withdrawals

Achievements and missions cleared while in debt are still **earned** - only the bonus waits.

pages.title: Recovery
pages.text:
Territory income keeps flowing and members can still deposit. The moment your balance reaches zero, bonuses are **restored automatically** and the Voice announces it.

There is no penalty beyond the time spent suspended.
*The practical advice: do not spend your buffer to zero right before a bill. A nation that buys a perk an hour before upkeep is a nation about to lose all its bonuses.*

categories.name: Systems
categories.description: The wider mechanics of the Elite Tensura world.

pages.text: Every chunk in the world holds **area magicule** - a living resource that rises where strong beings gather and fades where they don't. High-magicule chunks regenerate everyone's magicule faster, grow rare crystals, and can spawn tougher monsters.
Off by default - a server enables it with the **ETMagiculeWorldSystem** gamerule.

pages.title: Entity Influence
pages.text: Any living being with enough magicule (**50,000+**) raises the area magicule of the chunk it's standing in over time, up to a cap.
That bonus spreads into neighboring chunks and slowly fades once nothing strong lingers - a chunk's magicule rises and falls with who's actually there.

pages.title: Crystal Growth
pages.text: In high-magicule chunks, Magic Ore has a chance to slowly convert into Mother Rock. Mother Rock then sprouts Magic Ore crystal buds that grow through four stages - Small, Medium, Large, then Cluster - each stage drawing more from the chunk's magicule.

pages.title: Stronger Spawns
pages.text:
Natural mob spawns in very high-magicule chunks have a chance to be replaced by a tougher variant of the same monster.

Press **F8** to see a debug readout of the magicule in the chunk you're standing in.

Calamities, the Leviathan raid and the season's finale siege all pay out by **damage share** - and until now you only learned yours when the rewards landed.

The **Boss Contribution** panel shows it live, while the fight is still on.

The moment you land a hit on the boss, a small panel appears on the right of your screen: the **top three** damage dealers, plus your own row if you are not among them, each with damage dealt and share of the total. It refreshes every **two seconds**.

pages.title: Reading It
pages.text:
- A crown marks the current leader
- Your row is drawn in white, others in grey
- The bar under each row is that player's share of all damage so far
- Shares never shrink when the boss heals - they count lifetime damage, exactly as the payout does

pages.title: The Green Line
pages.text:
In a **calamity**, rewards need **10%** of the boss's health. Your bar starts grey with a white tick at that mark; cross it and the bar turns **green** - you qualify.

Raids and sieges pay by share alone, so their bars simply take the event's colour: teal for the Leviathan, red for the siege.

pages.title: Notes
pages.text:
- Only players who have damaged the boss see it - spectators never do
- Fighting two events at once? It follows whichever you hit last
- It fades about six seconds after the fight ends
- Move it from the mod list's **Config** button, under HUD Positions
- Servers can switch it off; there is no player toggle

Every so often (about every **15 minutes**, and only while at least **6** players are online) the server asks a **question in chat**.

You have about **30 seconds** to answer by typing. The **first** correct answer wins - everyone else gets nothing that round.
Answers match as a *substring*, so a sentence containing the answer counts. Nobody has to type it exactly.

pages.title: Speed Decides
pages.text:
Your reward depends entirely on **how fast** you answered:


- Within **5s** - **Elite Key**
- Within **15s** - **Rare Key**
- Any time after - **Common Key**
*That five-second window is the whole game. Speed matters far more than being the one who knew the answer.*

pages.title: Plushies
pages.text: Wins also earn **plushies**. Your **lifetime win count** unlocks tiers - the first plushie comes at **2** wins, then Uncommon at 8, Rare at 16, Epic at 25, Legendary at 30 - and every win from then on gives one random plushie:

- **Common** - 13 passive mobs
- **Uncommon** - 21, dolphins to iron golems
- **Rare** - 17 hostiles
- **Epic** - 15 nether and End mobs
- **Legendary** - 46, including the Ender Dragon, the Warden and the Tensura cast (Rimuru, Veldora, Velzard, Milim, Benimaru, Shuna, Shion, Souei, Hakurou, Kurobe, Diablo, Testarossa, Carrera, Ultima, Zegion, Apito, Kumara, Moss, Beretta, Ranga, Gobta, Gabiru, Treyni, Geld, Hinata, Guy Crimson, Leon, Luminous, Ramiris, Alvis, Albis, Suphia, Grucius, Eren, Gazel)

You always draw from your **highest** tier, so they get rarer as you win more.

pages.title: Collecting
pages.text: Plushies are decorative blocks - **114** variants, 112 of them in the trivia pools.

They are not craftable. Trivia is the main source, but **crates** roll them too - Common crates carry common plushies, Rare crates uncommon and rare ones, Elite crates epic and legendary (plus two crate-only extras).

If your inventory is full the plushie drops at your feet and can be picked up straight away.

Your win count is permanent and never resets.

**Crates** are loot boxes in three tiers - **Common**, **Rare**, and **Elite**. Each tier only opens with its own key.

Right-click a crate while holding its key to open it. The key is consumed and a roulette of possible rewards spins down onto what you won.

pages.title: Checking the Odds
pages.text: Not sure what you might win? **Hit** a crate, or right-click it with an **empty hand** - either one opens a preview of every possible reward and its exact drop chance. No key needed, nothing spent.

pages.title: Rewards
pages.text: Crates can drop items, skills, or Soul Points - and sometimes even *more keys* for a higher tier. Elite Crates hold the rarest loot in the game.

pages.title: Rarity & Pity
pages.text:
Every reward has a rarity - **Common**, **Uncommon**, **Rare**, **Epic** or **Legendary** - shown as a coloured bar in the preview.

Open a Common Crate 15 times without anything Rare or better and the next open is **guaranteed** Rare+. The preview counts it down.

A guaranteed pull is marked **PITY** on the reveal. Keys found inside crates never count as a hit, and creative mode does not track pity.

Rare and Elite Crates hand out Rare+ most of the time, so they ship with pity off - servers can turn it on.

pages.title: The Reveal
pages.text:
Higher rarities spin longer and climb through more colours before the flash. **Click anywhere** to skip straight to the result - you get the reward the moment it shows, skipped or not.

Epic and Legendary pulls set off fireworks at the crate for everyone nearby.

pages.title: Where Keys Come From
pages.text: Keys are not craftable. They come from other crates, **Calamity** payouts scaled by your contribution, and winning a **war** - every member of the winner gets a key, the top scorer a better one.
They also come from completing a **nation mission** (better still for clearing the whole cycle), chat trivia, and server events or admin grants.
*Each of the war, mission and calamity faucets can be toggled off by your server.*
With engravings, synergies, nation perks, season twists and transformations all pulling on the same blow, *what actually killed me* stops being an easy question.
The **Death Recap** answers it. When you die, a panel appears in the corner of the death screen listing your **last 8 hits**, oldest first.

pages.title: Reading It
pages.text:
Each line names what struck you, what kind of harm it was, and what the blow did:
- **5.0** - landed as it was
- **7.0 up 9.0** - something raised it
- **7.0 down 4.0** - something blunted it
- **negated** - it was turned aside entirely
Falling, drowning and fire show no attacker.

pages.title: What The Arrows Mean
pages.text: The arrow is the *whole* story of that blow - your resistances, your engravings, your synergies, the attacker's own gifts, whatever the season's twist is doing. It does not try to name which of them did what.
That is still enough. A hit landing at triple what you expected means something is feeding it. A defensive build showing no reduction at all is not working.

pages.title: Notes
pages.text:
- It covers everything - mobs, bosses, other players, the world itself
- Turned-aside blows still show, marked **negated** - useful proof a defence fired
- It clears itself when you leave the screen, so it never shows you an old death
- There is no button and no key. It simply happens, unless your server has switched it off.

When the server links a Discord, a **bridge** carries news between game and chat. It can post:
- World events - Calamities, awakenings
- Nation & diplomacy news
- Player milestones - records, achievements
- In-game chat
- Death messages

pages.title: Two-Way Chat
pages.text:
With the optional gateway bot running, messages typed in the linked Discord channel also appear **in-game** - a true two-way chat.

Everything here is controlled by the server and is off by default.

pages.title: Channel Commands
pages.text:
Type these straight into the linked Discord channel - the bot answers, and the message itself never crosses into game chat:
- **!list** - who's online
- **!tps** - server performance
- **!uptime** - how long the server has run

- **!leaderboard [board] [n]** - top players, one board or all of them
- **!nation <name>** - a nation's level, population, territory, standing and recent history
- **!season** - the current season number and top nations
- **!player <name>** - a player's nation, titles and playtime this week
*A server may rename the command prefix, disable individual commands, or turn the bot off entirely.*

A season does not simply stop. When it is called to an end, the world throws one last battle at whoever is still standing - the **Finale Siege**.

Win it and the season closes with spoils. Lose it and the season closes anyway, with nothing.

pages.title: The Waves
pages.text:
The siege is cried, then **10 minutes** pass so the living can gather.

**Four waves** of the undead follow. The first is **8** strong; each after adds **4** more and another quarter of health. A wave breaks early once **nine in ten** are dead, or after **5 minutes**.
The whole siege dies of old age after **45 minutes**.

pages.title: The Boss
pages.text:
After the last wave comes the **Lich** or the **Gravebound Colossus**, chosen blind, at **x3** health and **x2** damage.

There is nothing to join. Fight what comes. The world counts every blow each of you lands, and remembers who struck the last one.

pages.title: Spoils
pages.text:
If the boss falls:
- Top damage and the killer both take the **Siegebreaker** title
- Every wounder shares a **100 point** Legacy pool, split by damage, never less than 2
- Every nation that fought shares a **200 point** ladder pool

- The top **five** nations split **$50,000** in treasury

Nation spoils come from their own purse - being sworn to a nation never shrinks your own Legacy share.

pages.title: Failure
pages.text: If the clock runs out, or the last player logs off, the siege is lost. No title, no Legacy pool, no ladder points, no treasury.
The season still closes. Your Chronicle tiers, your leaderboard finishes and your nation's levels still become Legacy as always - only the siege's own spoils are forfeit.

The **Leaderboard** ranks players by their feats and writes the results onto the vanilla **scoreboard**, so standings are always on display.

Tracked boards include Awakened/EP, prestige Resets, Titles, Records, Nations, and Forge mastery.

pages.title: Checking Standings
pages.text:
Use */etleaderboard*:
- *awakened* - who has awakened, and their EP
- *resets* - prestige rankings
- *titles* / *records* / *nations*
- *forge* - crafting score & rarity
- *gui* - open the leaderboard screen

pages.title: Staying Listed
pages.text: Leaderboards only show **active** players: you must have been online at least **5 hours** (server-configurable) during this week or the last to appear.
Time counts automatically while you play. Fall below the requirement and you drop off the boards until you're active again - your scores are never lost, only hidden.
Everything you build in a season is unmade when it ends - your EP, your skills, your nation. **Legacy is the exception.**

Legacy Points are kept outside the world itself, so they outlive the wipe and follow you into every season after. They buy **cosmetics** - badges, an aura, and a few display titles that carry only modest, uncommon-grade bonuses. Legacy is a keepsake, not a power ladder.

pages.title: Earning Points
pages.text:
Paid once, at the season's close, for what you did:
- **10** per Chronicle tier completed
- **25** per top-three leaderboard slot held
- **2** per level your nation reached
- A share of **100** for damage dealt during the Finale Siege - waves and boss alike
A season where you cleared the Chronicle and topped a board is worth about 125 points. Most of the shop is several seasons deep.

pages.title: The Shop
pages.text: Codex, **Season** tab, **Legacy** section - your balance, what you own, what you wear.

Chat badges from **25** to **200** points, a pair of season-limited badges at **130**, three display titles from **90** to **220**, and one headline piece: the **Dawnrise Aura** at **350** - a glowing ring that plays every time you log in, sized to your character.

Servers may stock more.

pages.title: What You Keep
pages.text:
Bought is **yours forever**. Plushies and titles are handed back to you each new season when you log in - a world wipe never costs you a purchase.

Badges sit beside your name in chat. Wear one at a time, or none.
Some cosmetics can only be *bought* during a certain season. That limit never touches what is already in your collection.

If your server runs the **banking mod**, Elite Tensura ties into it.

Money becomes a real part of progression - it funds your nation's **treasury**, its levels and perks, war declarations, and the **contract board**.
*Without the banking mod none of this appears, and the rest of the addon works exactly as normal.*

pages.title: Cash from Mobs
pages.text:
Certain mobs drop **extra cash** when killed, on top of their usual loot.

*Subordinates and summons are exempt* - nobody can farm tamed or summoned mobs for money.

Which mobs pay out is set by your server.

pages.title: Auto-Pickup
pages.text:
Cash you pick up can be routed straight into your accounts instead of filling your inventory:


- **Off** - cash stays as items
- **Wallet** - goes to your wallet
- **Bank** - goes to your bank account
Pick your own mode with */etbank autopickup off|wallet|bank* - it starts on Off and remembers your choice. Bank falls back to Wallet if you have no primary account.
Auto-pickup also absorbs **money bills** dropped as items, whole bills only. The usual pickup popup can be suppressed by the server, so a long grind does not flood your screen.

pages.title: The Nation Tax
pages.text:
If you belong to a nation with an active treasury, a slice of every cash pickup is taxed - drawn from your primary bank account, so no account means no tax:


- **5%** to your nation's treasury
- **10%** into the central bank reserve

The second is a **money sink** - it leaves the economy entirely, keeping server-wide currency from inflating.

Both halves are suspended while your nation runs a *Tax Holiday* perk.
Every season rolls **one buff** and **one twist** when it starts. They hold for the whole season and bind everyone equally. The pair in force is shown in the **Season** tab of your Codex.
A mutator only rolls if the thing it touches is running - a calamity twist never appears where calamities are switched off.

pages.title: Kind Years
pages.text:
- **Surge of Souls** - kill EP x1.5
- **Generous World** - daily rewards x2
- **Restless Ambition** - one extra daily
- **Prosperous Trade** - mission and contract pay x1.5
- **Forgemaster's Favor** - one free perfect forge stage per Minecraft day

- **Magicule Bloom** - the land's magicule regrows x1.5 (needs the Magicule World system)
- **Enlightened Age** - mastery gain x1.5
- **Golden Age** - mob cash x2

pages.title: Hard Years
pages.text:
- **Magicule Drought** - the land's magicule regrows x0.5 (needs the Magicule World system)
- **Wrathful Calamities** - calamities x1.5 health, x1.25 damage
- **Heavy Crown** - nation upkeep x1.25
- **Cruel World** - hostile mobs +15% health, +10% damage

- **Demanding Chronicle** - daily targets x1.5
- **Age of Calamity** - calamities twice as often, one fewer player needed
- **Taxing Weave** - skill and magic costs x1.15

pages.title: Season Titles
pages.text: Thirteen titles can be earned **only** during a season, and most only under the twist that season rolled. A different twist simply never offers them. Two more - **Emberwrought** and **Second Dawn** - come from the top of the Second Dawn track.

- **Chronicler** - Bronze, Silver and Gold, for climbing the Chronicle deep
- **Drought-Blessed** - dailies cleared through the Drought
- **Iron Steward** - upkeep kept paid under a Heavy Crown

pages.title: Season Titles
pages.text:
- **Relentless** - every daily cleared, days running, under a Demanding Chronicle
- **Worldbreaker** - a long tally of kills in a Cruel World
- **Weave-Hardened** - enduring the Taxing Weave
- **Wrathbreaker** - standing against Wrathful Calamities

- **Calamity's Bane** - slaying in the Age of Calamity
- **Siegebreaker** - topping the Finale Siege

The greatest are cried across the whole server. What exactly they ask is never written down - that is the point of them.

A **season** is a run of the world with its own ladder laid over everything else you do. You climb a **Chronicle** of tiers, clear daily objectives, and when it ends the best players and nations are paid - then the world wipes and the next one begins.
Off by default - a server enables it with the **ETSeasonSystem** gamerule. If the Season tab is missing, no season is running.

pages.title: Where To Look
pages.text:
Open Tensura's main menu, click **Codex**, then the **Season** tab. It holds three things:
- **Chronicle** - your tier, its objectives, today's dailies
- **Legacy** - your points and the cosmetic shop
- **Nations** - the nation ladder standings
There is no season command for you to type. It is all in that tab.

pages.title: The Chronicle
pages.text:
A ladder of tiers. Each names several objectives and you must meet **all** of them.

Progress is read from your *lifetime* totals - the world wipes each season, so your lifetime is your season.
You never claim a tier. Satisfy it and it awards itself, announces you in chat, and banks points for your nation.

pages.title: First Flames
pages.text:
The default track runs ten tiers, climbing from Common Keys to Elite:
- **Awakening** - 500 kills, 5 biomes
- **Apprentice** - 10 forges, 100,000 EP, 5 records
- **Wayfarer** - 12 biomes, 5 structures
- **Blooded** - 8,000 kills, 5 titles

- **Veteran** - 10,000 kills, 10 titles
- **Calamity's Witness** - wound a calamity, 500,000 EP
- **Warforged** - 25 war kills, 50 forges
- **Ascending** - 5,000,000 EP, 15 records
- **Ascendant** - 50,000,000 EP, 25 records
- **Legend of the Season** - 250,000,000 EP, 3 calamities slain, 50 records, a war won

A second built-in track, **Second Dawn**, reshapes the ladder rather than simply raising it - gentler kill counts, an arena objective, two titles of its own, and an eleventh capstone tier for a tournament champion. Servers may run their own track entirely.

pages.title: Dailies
pages.text:
**Two** objectives are rolled for you each day - kills, forges, biomes, structures, records or titles.

They reset at **midnight UTC**, not your local midnight and not with nation upkeep. Clearing one pays a **Common Key** and banks points for your nation.
